title: Optic: one reader's research session
subtitle: A signed-in reader checks the day, reads a company's figures with their sources, asks Milo about one chart, saves a workspace, and opens it again on another computer
source: github.com/sidprobstein/optic at 34a30b7: pages/workspace.js, pages/financials.js, ui/inview.js, app/sparklines.py, app/insider_fill.py, app/layouts.py, app/usage.py; walked on the private test site

lanes.label: A reader
lanes.sub: signed in, follows a few stocks

steps.title: Home, during the session
steps.note: The reader opens Home while the market is open. Each ticker in the watchlist carries today's line, green or red by the day's direction, and says it is delayed.

steps.title: Five-minute bars
steps.note: Behind it, one request fetches every row's five-minute bars since the open, and again every five minutes.

steps.title: Presses 1D
steps.note: They press 1D on the headline chart and see today alone, with the price dot saying delayed.

steps.title: Opens Apple's Financials
steps.note: They open Apple and its Financials tab, and pick quarters. Opening a stock from Home is counted for the owner.

steps.title: Statements as charts
steps.note: Revenue, margins, cash flow and the balance sheet are drawn as charts by quarter, and under every chart a line says where the figures come from.

steps.title: Insider trades, 10 years
steps.note: Further down, they press 10 years on the insider trades and get the full history, not just the latest batch.

steps.title: SEC filings read
steps.note: The older trades are read from the company's own filings at the SEC in the background, each linked to its filing, and the table fills in as they arrive.

steps.title: Presses one chart
steps.note: They press the Cash flow by quarter chart, then Ask Milo in the top bar, and ask Milo to explain the chart.

steps.title: The answer is written
steps.note: Milo is told which chart they were looking at, with the figures on screen, and the answer is written about that chart.

steps.title: The answer
steps.note: In the answer, every reported figure is underlined with its source, and a line says the rest is Milo's reading of them.

steps.title: Arranges Home
steps.note: Back on Home, they put the news panel in its own colour group, so changing the main ticker leaves it alone, and name the layout.

steps.title: Saved on the account
steps.note: Save keeps the layout on their account, so it belongs to them rather than to one browser.

steps.title: Another computer
steps.note: On another computer, signed in, they open Saved layouts and their workspace comes back exactly as they left it.
steps.evidence: tests/e2e/test_pass2_workspace.py (a named layout saved in one browser opens in another)

steps.title: Counted, nothing personal
steps.sub: a visit, a stock, a question
steps.note: Along the way their visit, the stock opened from Home and the question to Milo were each counted, with no name and no question text.

steps.title: Opens Metrics
steps.note: Later, the owner opens Metrics and sees how many people opened a stock from Home, asked Milo, and came back.

journey.name: A reader checks the day, reads a company's figures, asks Milo about one chart, and keeps the workspace
journey.summary: One reader, start to finish, and the owner who reads the counts.
